Quirk Manifestation.text: Most Quirks appear in early childhood, usually by about age four. The first sign can be small: sparks from a fingertip, toys floating when a toddler cries, a sudden change in skin or hair. Mutant traits are often visible from birth and grow more pronounced over time. A first manifestation can be frightening and sometimes dangerous, and parents, preschools and pediatricians are trained to expect one. Late bloomers exist. A Quirk can stay hidden for years when its trigger never comes up, when it is too subtle to notice or when the body is not yet ready, and a rare few appear only in the teens or later. Doctors treat late onset as unusual but real, and the registry is updated when it happens. Quirks also grow. Strong emotion or sudden danger can push a Quirk past its usual limits for a moment, and everyone has heard stories of a power that doubled in a crisis. Those surges are real but costly and unreliable, and nobody builds a career on them. Steady growth comes from training, and it works at any age: control, range, output and endurance all improve with practice and a body conditioned to carry the power. Adults who begin serious training late can still make large gains, and hero academies expect every student's Quirk to change over three years of work.
